plan: Second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and risk-neutral bidders. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning at a price above my value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. No useful history (one round). My value is $10, so bid 10 to win only when the second-highest value is below 10 and pay that amount, yielding nonnegative surplus.

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks paying above value if the second-highest exceeds your value; underbidding risks losing when the price would have been profitable. With three rational bidders, others also bid truthfully. If we win, profit equals 30 minus the second-highest bid. Therefore, bid exactly our value. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies or beliefs. With rational opponents, they will also bid their true values. My value is 25, so bidding 25 ensures I win exactly when the second-highest value is below 25 and pay that second-highest bid, yielding nonnegative profit and no regret. ]
